title: From Prediction to Control
subtitle: An Atlas of Robot World Models
companion_to: From Prediction to Control: A Survey of Closed-Loop World Models for Robot Learning

roles.title: Representation
roles.definition: Learn task-relevant state or predictive features used by a downstream policy.

roles.title: Prediction and imagination
roles.definition: Predict consequences or futures for a decision or learning consumer.

roles.title: Simulation and data generation
roles.definition: Supply reusable generated interaction, demonstrations or training trajectories.

roles.title: Planning and search
roles.definition: Compare candidate actions, plans or skills using model outputs.

roles.title: Evaluation, reward and safety
roles.definition: Judge outcomes, policies, rewards or constraints using model information.

roles.title: Adaptation and monitoring
roles.definition: Use feedback to correct behavior, update context, request help or improve models and policies.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: The Prediction-to-Control Gap motivates a loop-centered survey. Predictive plausibility matters only through the decision or learning use it enables.
questions: What quantity is modeled?
Who consumes the output?
Which decision or learner changes?
chapters.boundary: Do not infer robot utility from visual realism alone.

chapters.title: Positioning Among Existing Surveys
chapters.summary: The survey relates architecture, application and world-model literature to a role-first account of robot learning.
questions: What does a related survey organize?
Which functional distinction does this survey add?
chapters.boundary: A role-based organization is not a claim that earlier surveys lacked functional categories.

chapters.title: A Robot Learning Loop View of World Models
chapters.summary: Read models through observation, action, predicted consequence, downstream consumer and returned execution feedback. Separate learning-time and execution-time loops.
questions: Can the predictor be queried under alternative actions?
Is the coupling to a learner or controller implemented?
Where does execution feedback enter?
chapters.boundary: Context refresh, action correction, policy learning and world-model weight updates are different forms of feedback.

chapters.title: The Optimizable Roles of World Models
chapters.summary: The six roles organize uses before architectures. A single system can serve several roles, and the same model can change roles when its consumer changes.
questions: What is the prediction objective?
What is the downstream use?
What object is changed by that use?
chapters.boundary: Roles describe interfaces and uses; they are neither disjoint model families nor maturity levels.

chapters.title: Representation Substrates and World-Model Mechanics
chapters.summary: Compare pixel/video, predictive latent, 3D/object-centric, structured physics and causal representations. RSSM, autoregression, diffusion, flow and ODE formulations are cross-cutting mechanics.
questions: Which state must be preserved for the task?
Which variables are action-grounded?
Does a claimed temporal mechanism refer to physical time or computation?
chapters.boundary: A causal-sounding objective is not identified causal structure. Continuous-time prediction need not accept queried candidate actions.

chapters.title: From Roles to Policy Improvement
chapters.summary: Imitation, offline RL, online model-based RL, planning and transfer consume model information differently. Track real and imagined experience separately.
questions: Is generated experience used for supervised learning or RL?
Is the world model frozen?
What feedback reaches the policy versus the model?
chapters.boundary: Synthetic trajectories alone do not establish online RL or deployment-time adaptation.

chapters.title: Foundation-Driven World Models and Robot Priors
chapters.summary: Foundation encoders, VLA proposals, imagination, neural simulation, rewards and constraint layers have distinct interfaces. Neural simulation can supply demonstrations, filtered BC data, policy optimization or evaluation.
questions: How are foundation priors adapted to robot actions?
What generated experience is selected or labeled?
What independent physical evidence supports utility?
chapters.boundary: Include adaptation, judging, resets and rejected samples in cost comparisons. A foundation policy alone is not a world model.

chapters.title: Tactile and Contact World Models
chapters.summary: Contact introduces hidden state, rate constraints and sensor-dependent representations. Separate predictive tactile control, world-action modeling, reactive policies and reusable sensing priors.
questions: Does tactile prediction change an action or learning target?
Is the contact loop executed online?
Which sensing transfer and retention tests are reported?
chapters.boundary: Predictive touch and direct tactile conditioning are different mechanisms. Keep OmniVTA and OmniVTLA distinct.

chapters.title: Human and Egocentric Data as a World-Model Source
chapters.summary: Human video can support representation priors, motion/action proxies, predictive world-action objectives or deployment context. Each route faces different grounding requirements.
questions: Which visual/sensing gap is addressed?
Which kinematic and contact gaps remain?
How are robot action labels obtained?
chapters.boundary: Human motion is not robot experience without grounding. Context conditioning and fast weight updates must be separated.

chapters.title: Embodiment and Task Perspective
chapters.summary: Manipulation stresses contact, navigation persistent belief, humanoids balance and morphology, driving traffic and rare events, and cross-robot control action semantics.
questions: What are the controller and action units?
What task history must persist?
Which physical feedback and assistance costs are measured?
chapters.boundary: A command-conditioned locomotion policy is not autonomous navigation. Open-loop physical execution is not online correction.

chapters.title: Evaluation: From Prediction Metrics to Closed-Loop Utility
chapters.summary: Report model behavior, policy effect, deployment behavior and evidence boundary. Model quality, policy utility and reliability are separate axes.
questions: Does the model preserve task-relevant consequences?
Does it improve the consumer under matched budgets?
Is feedback useful under induced policy queries?
chapters.boundary: Ranking correlation is not absolute calibration. Model-real disagreement alone does not diagnose model exploitation.

chapters.title: Resources: Datasets, Simulators, Benchmarks, and Frameworks
chapters.summary: Distinguish datasets, interactive engines, benchmark suites, harnesses and checkpoints. Check which interface an artifact actually provides.
questions: Can it support model fitting?
Can it branch decisions or learning trajectories?
Can it assess physical deployment and interventions?
chapters.boundary: Model, Decision, Learning and Deployment capabilities are non-nested. Static logs and a paper alone are not deployment resources.

chapters.title: Frontier Evidence Atlas: 2024–2026
chapters.summary: The frontier atlas locates emerging systems by mechanism, role and bounded evidence. It complements the historical bibliography without creating a pooled leaderboard.
questions: Which paper version supports the claim?
What hardware and task scope was tested?
Is the artifact availability separate from publication status?
chapters.boundary: Source evidence labels are curation judgments, not independently replicated rankings. Open-loop, frozen-model and policy-context cases stay explicit.

chapters.title: From Interaction to Model Improvement
chapters.summary: Organize the outer loop as acquisition, update target, retention, failure curation and fleet sharing. Record whether feedback changes context, policy, physical parameters, neural dynamics or memory.
questions: What data are acquired and under which policy?
Which learner receives each supervision signal?
What old-task behavior is retained?
chapters.boundary: A failed transition can teach dynamics while being an invalid behavior-cloning target. Actor RL and world-model SFT are different updates.

chapters.title: Open Challenges and Future Directions
chapters.summary: The agenda connects action grounding, multimodal contact, query-distribution shift, latency, memory, calibration and auditability to specific evaluation obligations.
questions: Which counterfactual queries reveal the gap?
Which matched-budget comparison can resolve it?
What evidence would overturn the proposed explanation?
chapters.boundary: Proposed utility curves, optimism gaps and reliability margins are research analyses, not measured universal findings.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.summary: The survey returns to a single criterion: whether a predictive interface contributes to better robot decisions and learning under its tested conditions.
questions: Which functional use is supported?
Where does physical feedback matter?
Which unresolved boundary changes the claim?
chapters.boundary: A larger model or richer video alone does not close the Prediction-to-Control Gap.

chapters.title: Extended Survey Protocols
chapters.summary: The appendix supplies role worksheets, reporting fields, reading paths and terminology for consistent curation.
questions: Can another reader reconstruct the interface?
Are source claim and editorial interpretation separated?
Is the evidence version and boundary explicit?
chapters.boundary: The worksheet supports an audit; filling fields does not validate scientific claims.

curated.name: World Models
curated.interface: A compressed visual state and recurrent predictive dynamics.
curated.consumer_and_change: A controller consumes the learned state and predictive environment.
curated.boundary: Early non-robot control evidence supplies conceptual background; do not infer general robot deployment.

curated.name: PlaNet
curated.interface: Action-conditioned latent dynamics predict future states and rewards.
curated.consumer_and_change: Online planning selects actions through imagined latent trajectories.
curated.boundary: Separate model fit, planning cost and downstream control performance.

curated.name: Dreamer
curated.interface: A latent dynamics model supplies imagined trajectories.
curated.consumer_and_change: Actor and value learning use imagination; the deployed actor can act without an explicit rollout planner.
curated.boundary: Learning-time imagination and execution-time replanning are different interfaces.

curated.name: DreamerV2
curated.interface: Discrete latent dynamics support imagined behavior learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Imagination updates the actor and value function.
curated.boundary: Atari evidence is methodological context, not physical robot validation.

curated.name: DreamerV3
curated.interface: A latent world model supports behavior learning across domains.
curated.consumer_and_change: Model-generated trajectories train behavior and value estimates.
curated.boundary: Cross-domain success does not remove embodiment, contact or real-time evaluation requirements.

curated.name: Dreamer4
curated.interface: Scalable world-model-generated experience for agent training.
curated.consumer_and_change: Policies learn inside a predictive environment.
curated.boundary: Distinguish scalable agent-training evidence from robot-specific action grounding and hardware transfer.

curated.name: DayDreamer
curated.interface: A learned predictive model uses physical robot interaction data.
curated.consumer_and_change: Imagined experience supports robot policy learning.
curated.boundary: Robot and task conditions bound the results; physical learning does not imply universal embodiment transfer.

curated.name: TD-MPC2
curated.interface: Latent predictive dynamics and value estimates support continuous control.
curated.consumer_and_change: Model-predictive control selects actions.
curated.boundary: Report action-space, horizon and compute settings rather than comparing raw success across unrelated tasks.

curated.name: DINO-WM
curated.interface: Action-conditioned prediction operates on pretrained visual features.
curated.consumer_and_change: Planning consumes predicted features to select controls.
curated.boundary: Visual feature pretraining alone is not action-grounded dynamics or proof of closed-loop utility.

curated.name: V-JEPA 2
curated.interface: Video predictive representations are adapted for action-conditioned use.
curated.consumer_and_change: A planning consumer connects predictions to robotic decisions.
curated.boundary: Keep generic video pretraining separate from the action-conditioned robot adaptation experiment.

curated.name: ACT-JEPA
curated.interface: A joint-embedding predictive objective learns policy-relevant representations.
curated.consumer_and_change: Representation learning affects downstream policy learning.
curated.boundary: A predictive representation objective does not by itself establish online action search.

curated.name: Causal-JEPA
curated.interface: Object-level latent masking learns predictive dependencies.
curated.consumer_and_change: Downstream uses consume object-aware predictive representations.
curated.boundary: The name does not establish identification of a causal graph or valid causal interventions.

curated.name: ODEWorld
curated.interface: Observation- and goal-conditioned prediction uses continuous physical-time flow.
curated.consumer_and_change: The interface predicts futures at physical-time queries.
curated.boundary: The reviewed interface does not accept queried candidate actions; do not label it an action-intervention planner.

curated.name: PointWorld
curated.interface: A 3D point-based world model predicts action consequences.
curated.consumer_and_change: MPPI planning produces robot action sequences.
curated.boundary: The reported physical execution is open loop; model inference time excludes the full planning pipeline.

curated.name: PhysTwin
curated.interface: Video observations inform structured deformable-object physics reconstruction.
curated.consumer_and_change: The reconstructed simulation supports interaction reasoning.
curated.boundary: Physics reconstruction and a complete learned robot control loop require separate evidence.

curated.name: WorldPlanner
curated.interface: Action-conditioned visual prediction supports search over futures.
curated.consumer_and_change: Global Monte Carlo tree search and local MPC choose actions.
curated.boundary: Learned-state PushT comparisons and demonstration baselines should not be treated as a common cross-paper leaderboard.

curated.name: Large Video Planner
curated.interface: Generated visual plans are converted into executable robot motion.
curated.consumer_and_change: Retargeting produces actions for physical execution.
curated.boundary: Plan generation and retargeting are followed by open-loop execution; do not infer real-time feedback correction.

curated.name: RoboDreamer
curated.interface: Compositional robot imagination predicts visual task futures.
curated.consumer_and_change: Predicted futures provide a task-facing imagination interface.
curated.boundary: Compositional generation must be assessed separately from decision coupling and execution feedback.

curated.name: Robotic World Model (RWM)
curated.interface: A learned neural simulator predicts robot interaction consequences.
curated.consumer_and_change: MBPO-PPO optimizes policies using model-generated experience.
curated.boundary: The studied pipeline uses physics-simulator data and interactions; hardware transfer is not simulator-free training.

curated.name: Interactive World Simulator (IWS)
curated.interface: An interactive predictive environment supports demonstrations and evaluation.
curated.consumer_and_change: Generated demonstrations train downstream robot policies.
curated.boundary: Equal demonstration-set sizes exclude world-model construction cost and do not establish online RL.

curated.name: Hi-WM
curated.interface: Rollback and branching inside a world model enable targeted human corrections.
curated.consumer_and_change: Corrected trajectories support robot policy post-training.
curated.boundary: The mechanism uses human correction; gains do not establish unattended synthetic data collection.

curated.name: GE-Sim 2.0
curated.interface: Video prediction is coupled to proprioceptive state and task-feedback modules.
curated.consumer_and_change: Successful-rollout filtering supplies behavior-cloning updates.
curated.boundary: The cited physical improvement is filtered supervised learning, not an online-RL experiment.

curated.name: GeniWorld
curated.interface: Rendered robot motion grounds action-conditioned visual prediction.
curated.consumer_and_change: Synthetic condition augmentation supports policy improvement.
curated.boundary: The reported overall average mixes standard and OOD settings; it is not an OOD-only score.

curated.name: DreamGen
curated.interface: Video-generated behavior is paired with recovered pseudo-actions.
curated.consumer_and_change: Synthetic demonstrations supply policy-training supervision.
curated.boundary: Pseudo-action recovery and trajectory validity are essential; video quality alone is not training utility.

curated.name: DreamDojo
curated.interface: Large-scale human video supplies interaction priors adapted to robot controls.
curated.consumer_and_change: Adapted world-model rollouts support robot-facing uses.
curated.boundary: Human-video scale does not resolve the robot action, dynamics and contact gaps without grounding.

curated.name: WoVR
curated.interface: Action-conditioned rollouts use critical-state initialization and alignment.
curated.consumer_and_change: RL post-trains VLA policies in the predictive simulator.
curated.boundary: Keep manuscript-cited v2 results and per-platform averages separate from other versions and hardware.

curated.name: RoboWorld
curated.interface: Neural simulation predicts outcomes for generalist robot policy evaluation.
curated.consumer_and_change: Generated outcomes rank or assess policies.
curated.boundary: High model-to-real correlation is neither absolute calibration nor demonstrated policy-training gain.

curated.name: WorldEval
curated.interface: Policy-conditioned video prediction is combined with a separate task verifier.
curated.consumer_and_change: Evaluation compares robot policy checkpoints.
curated.boundary: Evaluation evidence does not establish that the same model improves policies through training.

curated.name: VLA-RFT
curated.interface: A world simulator and verified rewards supply policy-learning feedback.
curated.consumer_and_change: GRPO updates the VLA policy while the world model is frozen.
curated.boundary: Policy fine-tuning must not be described as online world-model weight adaptation.

curated.name: World-Gymnast
curated.interface: Language tasks and edited scenes expand a predictive training environment.
curated.consumer_and_change: RL updates robot policies using generated task experience.
curated.boundary: Generated tasks must remain executable and independently judgeable; trajectory count is not coverage.

curated.name: Cosmos
curated.interface: Pretrained world-model components supply physical-domain generation priors.
curated.consumer_and_change: Robot-specific adaptation can consume these priors.
curated.boundary: A general foundation platform is not, by itself, a demonstrated closed-loop robot system.

curated.name: Cosmos 3
curated.interface: Omnimodal world modeling broadens physical-domain predictive interfaces.
curated.consumer_and_change: Downstream embodied systems can adapt the learned priors.
curated.boundary: Separate broad modality coverage from action grounding and measured robot policy utility.

curated.name: Genie
curated.interface: A learned generative environment supports interactive visual futures.
curated.consumer_and_change: Agents can consume an interactive generated environment.
curated.boundary: Latent interaction interfaces require robot-control grounding before robot deployment claims.

curated.name: Manipulation by Feel
curated.interface: Tactile observations and actions feed a deep predictive model.
curated.consumer_and_change: Model-predictive control uses touch predictions to choose actions.
curated.boundary: Sensor, contact and manipulation conditions define the control evidence.

curated.name: RoboPack
curated.interface: Tactile-informed dynamics encode latent physical interaction state.
curated.consumer_and_change: Predicted contact dynamics support dense-packing decisions.
curated.boundary: The learned physical representation should be judged through the downstream planning task.

curated.name: VIRDO++
curated.interface: Visuo-tactile implicit representations capture deformable-object state and dynamics.
curated.consumer_and_change: Predictive perception provides deformable-state estimates.
curated.boundary: Representation and dynamics evidence do not automatically establish a complete robot policy improvement loop.

curated.name: ContactWorld
curated.interface: Vision-tactile latent world modeling studies contact-relevant predictive representations.
curated.consumer_and_change: Contact-aware representations support manipulation-facing predictions.
curated.boundary: Compare contact prediction and downstream control separately; a representation study is not a general contact guarantee.

curated.name: OmniVTA
curated.interface: A visuo-tactile predictive model is paired with fast tactile feedback.
curated.consumer_and_change: A reflex interface corrects actions during contact-rich manipulation.
curated.boundary: Feedback-driven action correction is distinct from online neural weight updates; OmniVTLA is a different system.

curated.name: Visuo-Tactile World Models
curated.interface: Joint visual and tactile prediction informs future interaction estimates.
curated.consumer_and_change: A planning interface produces contact-rich robot actions.
curated.boundary: The reviewed plan execution is open loop; avoid labeling it online corrective control.

curated.name: DexTacWAM
curated.interface: Visuo-tactile world-action modeling couples predictive touch with dexterous action learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Predictive tactile supervision influences dexterous manipulation policies.
curated.boundary: Direct tactile conditioning is a comparator, not the same mechanism; evidence remains task- and platform-bounded.

curated.name: VTAM
curated.interface: Video, tactile and action modeling connects visual futures to contact information.
curated.consumer_and_change: The joint predictive-action interface supports physical interaction.
curated.boundary: Visual prediction, tactile prediction and policy utility need separate ablations.

curated.name: VT-WAM
curated.interface: Visual-tactile world-action modeling learns coupled contact futures and actions.
curated.consumer_and_change: Action generation consumes multimodal predictive information.
curated.boundary: World-action modeling does not by itself demonstrate online corrective planning or sensor transfer.

curated.name: Dream-Tac
curated.interface: A unified tactile world-action model represents contact-rich predictive-action relationships.
curated.consumer_and_change: The learned action interface supports manipulation.
curated.boundary: Keep predictive supervision distinct from direct tactile conditioning and real-time deployment evidence.

curated.name: Tactile-WAM
curated.interface: Asymmetric attention integrates tactile signals into world-action modeling.
curated.consumer_and_change: Touch-aware predictive-action features influence actions.
curated.boundary: Asymmetric training access and actual deployment sensor access must be reported separately.

curated.name: Sparsh
curated.interface: Self-supervised learning provides tactile feature representations.
curated.consumer_and_change: Downstream sensing and policy systems consume the features.
curated.boundary: A tactile representation prior is contextual; predictive control requires an additional action-grounded model and consumer.

curated.name: AnyTouch
curated.interface: Static and dynamic visuo-tactile representation learning spans multiple sensors.
curated.consumer_and_change: Downstream systems reuse tactile features.
curated.boundary: Sensor representation transfer is not proof of transferred robot predictive dynamics.

curated.name: OmniVTLA
curated.interface: A vision-tactile-language-action policy consumes semantically aligned tactile sensing.
curated.consumer_and_change: The learned policy predicts actions.
curated.boundary: Keep this policy distinct from the predictive-reflex world-model system OmniVTA.

curated.name: MuSe
curated.interface: Force sensing is added to pretrained visuomotor policies through continual learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Policy adaptation incorporates new sensory information.
curated.boundary: Continual sensory adaptation is related context; validate retention and predictive dynamics separately.

curated.name: Gen2Act
curated.interface: Generated human videos provide novel task scenarios for robot learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: A robot-learning pipeline consumes generated behavior supervision.
curated.boundary: Human motion must be grounded in robot sensing, kinematics and executable actions.

curated.name: Dreamitate
curated.interface: Video generation supplies visuomotor policy-learning experience.
curated.consumer_and_change: Generated supervision updates robot policies.
curated.boundary: Generated demonstrations are a learning-time route, not proof of online model-based planning.

curated.name: EgoWAM
curated.interface: Egocentric human data supply a world-action modeling objective beyond pixels.
curated.consumer_and_change: A predictive-action learner transfers information to robot behavior.
curated.boundary: The visual, kinematic, dynamics/contact and action-label gaps remain distinct evaluation obligations.

curated.name: AnyWorld
curated.interface: Factorized egocentric modeling recomposes observations, instructions and actions.
curated.consumer_and_change: Recomposition supplies missing training combinations for cross-embodiment use.
curated.boundary: Broad recombination is not automatic physical validity or universal embodiment transfer.

curated.name: Zero-WAM
curated.interface: Human-video context conditions world-action modeling at test time.
curated.consumer_and_change: Context changes the predictions and generated actions.
curated.boundary: In-context adaptation must not be described as test-time neural weight training.

curated.name: WAM-TTT
curated.interface: Human play at test time steers a world-action model through adaptation.
curated.consumer_and_change: Test-time learning changes fast model weights.
curated.boundary: Distinguish weight updates from Zero-WAM context conditioning and account for adaptation cost.

curated.name: TactAlign
curated.interface: Tactile alignment supports transfer from human interaction to robot policies.
curated.consumer_and_change: The transferred policy uses contact-related information.
curated.boundary: Policy transfer is not evidence that a robot predictive dynamics model transferred.

curated.name: EgoZero
curated.interface: Smart-glasses human interaction supplies robot-learning information.
curated.consumer_and_change: The robot policy is trained using grounded human-derived supervision.
curated.boundary: Egocentric video is not an executable robot trajectory until action and embodiment gaps are addressed.

curated.name: VLAW
curated.interface: Real interaction refines a world model that supplies synthetic policy-training data.
curated.consumer_and_change: Iterative model and policy improvement changes both learners through distinct updates.
curated.boundary: Weighted supervised policy updates with an RL interpretation must not be relabeled PPO or GRPO.

curated.name: WorldSample
curated.interface: Counterfactual world-model transitions supplement real robot RL experience.
curated.consumer_and_change: Online policy learning consumes real and selectively generated transitions.
curated.boundary: Report transition provenance, uncertainty scheduling and matched real-interaction budgets.

curated.name: WAM-RL
curated.interface: Reconstruction rewards support actor learning while online video supervision updates the world model.
curated.consumer_and_change: Actor RL and world-model video SFT change different parameter sets.
curated.boundary: Do not collapse the separate objectives and KL constraints into a single joint RL loss.

curated.name: Model-Based Runtime Monitoring
curated.interface: A predictive model estimates problematic policy outcomes during deployment.
curated.consumer_and_change: A monitor requests human intervention; later interaction supports learning.
curated.boundary: Detection, human decisions and subsequent retraining are separate events.

curated.name: Sirius-Fleet
curated.interface: Visual prediction supports multi-task interactive robot-fleet learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Monitoring and human assistance influence collection and policy improvement.
curated.boundary: The reviewed predictor is frozen and does not query alternative candidate actions; fleet learning is not online dynamics adaptation.

curated.name: REGEN
curated.interface: Generative replay retains prior task experience during continual imitation learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Replayed experience supports policy retention as new tasks arrive.
curated.boundary: Replay quality and task retention need empirical checks; generation alone does not guarantee lifelong learning.

curated.name: Planning with Online World Models
curated.interface: Interaction updates a world model used for planning during continual learning.
curated.consumer_and_change: Feedback can change predictive parameters and later decisions.
curated.boundary: Report update cadence, query distribution and old-task retention rather than treating any update as beneficial.

curated.name: WorldArena
curated.interface: A benchmark examines perceptual quality and embodied functional utility.
curated.consumer_and_change: Evaluation protocols compare model behavior and decision utility.
curated.boundary: The benchmark is an evaluation resource, not a robot world-model method or a universal deployment certificate.

curated.name: EWMBench
curated.interface: Evaluation probes scene, motion and semantic quality in embodied world models.
curated.consumer_and_change: Quality tests assess predictive outputs.
curated.boundary: Perceptual and semantic quality do not substitute for downstream policy improvement.

curated.name: World-in-World
curated.interface: A closed-loop benchmarking interface connects model predictions to agent interaction.
curated.consumer_and_change: Online planning protocols assess generated environments.
curated.boundary: Task scope and action APIs determine applicability; the benchmark name does not establish robot hardware evidence.

curated.name: SafeDreamer
curated.interface: A learned world model supplies predicted trajectories for Lagrangian-based constrained planning.
curated.consumer_and_change: World-model planning consumes task and safety information to choose actions.
curated.boundary: The inspected upstream account reports Safety-Gymnasium experiments; constraint satisfaction is conditional on the tested environment, model and reporting protocol.

curated.name: OpenVLA
curated.interface: A foundation vision-language-action policy maps observations and instructions to actions.
curated.consumer_and_change: It supplies a policy baseline or consumer for world-model training and evaluation.
curated.boundary: A VLA policy is not a world model solely because it predicts actions.

curated.name: pi0
curated.interface: A flow-based vision-language-action foundation policy generates robot controls.
curated.consumer_and_change: It supplies an action policy or downstream world-model consumer.
curated.boundary: Action generation alone does not satisfy action-intervenable consequence prediction.

curated.name: GR00T N1.7
curated.interface: A reasoning VLA foundation model provides humanoid-facing action proposals.
curated.consumer_and_change: Downstream embodied systems consume its policy interface.
curated.boundary: Reasoning and generalist policy capabilities do not automatically establish a predictive robot world model.
